anchor_comparisons: The counter anchor's 7.77-9.87 band is relevant because contract terms and customer-level allocation remain unverifiable, but current issuer-stated orders and completed arrangements support a value modestly above that band.

The positive anchor's 14.28-16.38 band requires more durable and auditable conversion than is shown while LTA pricing can lag, performance reviews affect allocation and customer product delays reduce contribution.
disagreements: The memo midpoint overstates contract quality because the binding economic terms are not externally auditable.
Sold-out planned capacity and purchase orders do not establish realized shipment timing or cash collection when customer schedules can move.
payload.rationale: Every counterfact impairs the quality or timing of visibility. NDA prevents validation of quantity, price, cancellation and minimum-purchase terms; long-term arrangements can delay market-price realization; customer performance reviews condition allocation; and downstream product delays have already reduced expected contribution. Positive facts show demand and orders, but the 30% statistic covers memory broadly and the customer-official technology mention is neither qualification nor a purchase contract.
payload.why_not_higher: There is no customer-level committed volume, price, cancellation protection, allocation history or realized shipment bridge, and customer schedule delay is already a current counterfact.
payload.why_not_lower: The record is stronger than a weak-visibility profile because issuer statements identify purchase orders, completed longer-term arrangements and sold-out planned capacity rather than only pipeline interest.
